sections.overview: A small marine snailfish in the family Liparidae, it is known from the eastern Pacific off Mexico and the United States.
sections.identification: Its mouth and lower jaw are unusually steeply angled; the species name refers to this nearly vertical profile.
sections.habitat: Records place it in deep water, but collection depths are difficult to interpret because specimens were taken in midwater above very deep seafloor.
sections.diet: The consulted species accounts do not document its diet.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior has not been described in the consulted accounts.
sections.reproduction: The consulted accounts provide no species-specific reproductive information.
sections.ecology: Only a few specimens are reported, so its ecology remains poorly known. Like P. islandicus, it is described with a sharply angled mouth; P. islandicus is recorded south of Iceland in the northeast Atlantic, while this species is eastern Pacific. P. dentatus is another eastern-Pacific congener, distinguished in its description by unusually large, inward-curving teeth.
sections.conservation: The consulted FishBase page lists the species as not evaluated by the IUCN.
